diagnosis.operation_cpu: No added reservation CPU work is demonstrated inside measure_one: candidate Ir, Dr and Dw are lower in all five cells (Float e1 -1.594%, e2 -2.246%, e8 -2.390%, e32 -4.913%, NoHeadFoot e32 -5.424%).
diagnosis.operation_cache: Simulated D1 read/write misses are lower in every cell; candidate Float e32 DLmw=921 versus baseline 1 is an isolated LLd write-miss anomaly and is not treated as native latency evidence.
diagnosis.publication: At Float e02, inclusive Package::render_with_layout and candidate OleWriter::write_to_vec Ir are lower than the baseline Package::render_with_layout and OleWriter::write_to rows; the candidate does not show a scoped publication instruction increase.
diagnosis.native_context: Whole-process perf samples are dominated by libc memmove, glibc malloc/free, DOC sprm parsing and SHA compression. This identifies copy/allocator work as the useful next boundary but cannot assign those samples to the reservation path.
diagnosis.page_faults: One-child perf stat shows candidate page-fault deltas of +154.219%/+8.146%/-2.301%/+22.335%/-27.746% for Float e1/e2/e8/e32 and NoHeadFoot e32. Retained 12-round receipts are highly variable: paired median deltas are +216.01%, +80.43%, -11.85%, +45.02%, -3.41%; these are whole-process context, not proof of an operation-local cause.
diagnosis.syscalls: The corrected strace controls show no consistent syscall increase: total calls are baseline/candidate 304/300 (Float e2), 506/598 (Float e32), and 338/274 (NoHeadFoot e32).
diagnosis.next_profile_hypothesis: If diagnosis resumes, inspect source-line and branch/copy costs around Package::render_with_layout and write_to_vec together with page residency/allocator placement under a separately controlled launch. The retained evidence supports libc copy/allocator placement and launch-level page mapping as hypotheses for Float1/2/32 and the marginal Float8 timing result, not a reservation-loop CPU regression.
diagnosis.adoption: No production adoption recommendation; 0920 rejection remains unchanged.
